alt.en: The top of a printed map in buff and grey of a wide bay, dotted with depth soundings. At upper left, the ornate title "The Key to East Virginia". At upper centre, a star-shaped fort marked "Fortress Monroe" stands at the tip of a spit of land below the town of Hampton. Across the water at lower right, a point of land is marked "Sewalls Point".
alt.es: La parte superior de un mapa impreso en ocre y gris de una bahía ancha, salpicada de cifras de profundidad. Arriba a la izquierda, el título adornado "The Key to East Virginia". Arriba en el centro, un fuerte en forma de estrella marcado "Fortress Monroe" en la punta de una lengua de tierra, bajo la ciudad de Hampton. Al otro lado del agua, abajo a la derecha, una punta de tierra marcada "Sewalls Point".

caption.en: Fortress Monroe on a map published in New York in 1861, across Hampton Roads from Sewell's Point, where, the National Park Service writes, Frank Baker, Shepard Mallory and James Townsend were made to build Confederate gun positions before they fled to the fort in May 1861.
caption.es: Fortress Monroe en un mapa publicado en Nueva York en 1861, al otro lado de Hampton Roads frente a Sewell's Point, donde, según el Servicio de Parques Nacionales, Frank Baker, Shepard Mallory y James Townsend fueron obligados a construir posiciones de artillería confederadas antes de huir al fuerte en mayo de 1861.

source: The key to East Virginia showing the exact relative positions of Fortress Monroe, Rip Raps, Newport News, Sewalls [sic] Point, Norfolk, Gosport Navy Yard and expressing the soundings of every part of Hampton Roads & Elizabeth River, compiled from government surveys and drawn by M. K. Couzens (New York: W. Schaus, c1861), top part
library: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division
licenceEvidence: Published New York: W. Schaus, c1861 (LoC catalogue record https://lccn.loc.gov/99439180, field 260 "New York, W. Schaus, c1861."); stamped "Nov. 15, 1861" on the sheet. Drawn by M. K. Couzens, civil engineer (death year not found; a map-maker at work in 1861 cannot have lived to 1955). PD in the US (published before 1931), the EU and Israel (life + 70 long run out). Scan of the LoC copy taken from Wikimedia Commons, which marks it PD-Art / PD-old-100-1923 and names the LoC as source (see rights.md).
credit: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division

alt.en: A printed book page headed "22 Jubilee Songs." and, in black-letter type, "Go down, Moses.", with four lines of music in four parts on two staves, in 4/4 time with four flats, the first verse and the refrain under the notes, and verses 2, 3 and 4 printed below.
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro con el encabezado "22 Jubilee Songs." y, en letra gótica, "Go down, Moses.", con cuatro sistemas de música a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas, en 4/4 y con cuatro bemoles, la primera estrofa y el estribillo bajo las notas, y debajo las estrofas 2, 3 y 4.

caption.en: Go down, Moses on page 22 of Jubilee Songs (New York, 1872), as the Fisk Jubilee Singers sang it, with the leader's calls printed for the tune alone and every "Let my people go", like the refrain, for four voices: the page our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: Go down, Moses en la página 22 de Jubilee Songs (Nueva York, 1872), tal como la cantaban los Fisk Jubilee Singers, con las llamadas de quien dirige impresas para la melodía sola y cada "Let my people go", como el estribillo, a cuatro voces: la página de la que se lee nuestro arreglo.

source: Jubilee Songs: As Sung by the Jubilee Singers of Fisk University (Nashville, Tenn.) under the Auspices of the American Missionary Association (New York: Biglow & Main, 1872), p. 22, "Go down, Moses."
library: Emory University, Manuscript, Archives and Rare Book Library (digitized for the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1872; Seward died 1902, White died 1895. Emory's record: "The online edition of this book in the public domain, i.e., not protected by copyright, has been produced by the Emory University Digital Library Publications Program" (https://archive.org/details/29208201.4853.emory.edu). Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
